name: Bram Hollis

loved: {item}! Friend, you've got taste. First round's on me.
Ha! {item}! The cellar will smell like heaven tonight.
disliked: {item}? Hm. I'll find someone who wants it.
hated: I run a clean kitchen! Take it away!

arrival: Well, hello! Bram Hollis, innkeeper. Or I was, before the last town dried up.

arrival.say: I see you've got a place with barrels and a fire. Looks like a tavern in the making. Can an old cook stay on?

choices.text: Please do. The village needs a heart.
reply: Ha! I'll try to be a warm one.
Deal. Eggs, bacon, and a story with every plate.

arrival: I'll fetch my pans. Come by later. First pint's free.
bouquet_reject: Ha! Flattering. But my heart belongs to the kitchen, friend, and to a lady long gone.

greetings.say: It's my birthday? Ha, don't remind an old man. Come, have a drink!
The usual? I remember the usual.
Rain's good for business. Folk want soup.
Breakfast shift! Eggs are hot, gossip's hotter.
Evenings are for stories. Got one for you, if you've got time.
{player}, my friend! You always bring good luck through that door.

script: Ah, {player}! Perfect timing. I've got a new stew and I need an honest mouth.
*He ladles a bowl and slides it across the bar, steaming.*

reply: HA! Everyone says that! ...Fine, you win. A pinch more.
Now you're just buttering me up. ...Keep going.
A chef never reveals the sauce. But... carrots. Mostly carrots.

script: *A broad traveler is slumped on the bar, loud and swaying. Bram catches your eye.*
Psst. {player}. Could use a hand with this one.

script.say: He's had enough, but he won't hear it from me. Any ideas?

choices.text: Step in and escort him out.
reply: *The traveler grumbles but goes quietly with a clap on his back.*

choices.text: Pour him a big glass of water.
reply: Water. Brilliant. I should've thought of it.
Ha. Fair enough. Not everyone's cut out for the bar.

script: *Evening. The room is quiet. Bram wipes the same mug over and over.*
I wasn't always a cook, {player}. I guarded caravans for twelve years.
One night we were ambushed on the pass. I lost four friends. I walked away with a limp and a nightmare.

script.say: That's why I'm here. I wanted to build somewhere nobody has to be afraid on the road.

reply: *He sets down the mug. His eyes are shiny.* Hm. Maybe I have.
Nobody's asked in years. Thank you.
*He goes back to wiping the mug.* Easy to say.

script: *The tavern door is closed. A new sign hangs above it, still swinging.*
I know it's supposed to be a surprise, but I can't wait. Look up.
*It reads: 'The Hearth & Stranger.' In the lower corner, small, there's one more symbol: your initial.*

script.say: Every inn needs a stranger who became a friend. I couldn't have put anyone else in that corner.

reply: *He claps your shoulder.* The honour's mine. Free pints for life.
